newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:
Spokesman Peter Guilford said the Commission had decided to reintroduce minimum prices on computer chips originating from Japan and Korea.

In answer to a question, spokesman Jean-Christophe Filori said the Transport Council would discuss the negotiations with Switzerland on transport. He also said an agreement could be reached in the next few months.
Spokeswoman Heike Gerstbrein said the Commission would look into ways to prevent companies abusing the structural funds system by moving their activities to eligible regions.

Asked about the summertime directive, Filori said it expired this year. He said a member state could have a derogation from the directive if the Council agreed. He said a decision would need a qualified majority vote.

Guilford said Chinese accession to the World Trade Organisation could happen before the end of 1997 if there was sufficient political will on all sides to achieve such a result. He said the EU would respond in a positive way if China moved sufficiently. He also said that discussions were "so far, so good".
Spokesman Gerry Kieley said there would be a conference on meat and animal meal in June.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/195: Strong support for Romania's reform package.
- IP/97/196: Signature of the EU/Morocco financing convention.
- IP/97/197: Statement of Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies on the movement of companies.
- IP/97/198: EU announces gradual reintroduction of minimum prices on computer chips.
- Speech/97/56: Speech by Commissioner Franz Fischler on "EU common agricultural policy achievements and challenges ahead".
- Speech/97/57: Speech by Commissioner Edith Cresson on "teaching and learning in the information society".
- Speech/97/58: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on "current aspects of the EU: a view from the European Commission".
- Business and consumer surveys - first results: February 1997 No 2.
